dedupe_keys.name: solem space debris long term evolution model

description: SOLEM is the first long-term space debris evolution model of China. The paper by Xiao-Wei Wang and Jing Liu, posted on arXiv in March 2019, describes its principles, components and workflow, analyses the effects of different mitigation measures on the future debris population with it, and states its limitations and a plan for improvement. Like other evolutionary models it projects how the population of objects in Earth orbit grows under launch, collision, explosion and decay, so that mitigation policies such as post-mission disposal can be compared. Coverage is the whole Earth-orbit environment over decades. Format and access: the paper is openly available; no code or executable release was found. Licence: the paper is CC BY 4.0; the model itself is not released; free to read. Caveats: the method can be reused only from the description, and validation against other models is limited to what the paper reports. It supports hazard exposure and capacity planning studies of orbital debris for satellite infrastructure. Related catalogue records are NASA's LEGEND evolutionary model and ESA's MASTER environment model.
